line: # Alphabet summary from byrom1796_alphabet_p12.jpg, "On the Consonants":
# b = a closing-parenthesis-like curve, and also a small hook (two forms given)
# d = an open-parenthesis-like curve "("
# f or v = a single diagonal stroke "\" (top-left to bottom-right)
# g = a small looping swirl
# h = two small hook/loop marks (two forms given)
# j = two small curved marks (two forms given)
# k or c hard = a single small hook
# l = three curly stroke forms
# m = a single backward-hook stroke
# n = a small "u"/smile-shaped curve
# p = a closing-parenthesis-like curve ")"
# q = a hooked stroke with a short descender
# r = a single diagonal stroke "/" (bottom-left to top-right)
# s or c soft, and z = a short horizontal dash "-"
# t = a single vertical stroke "|"
# w = two small hook/loop marks (two forms given)
# x = two marks, one check-shaped and one hooked
# y = a single tilde-like hook
# ch = a single backward-curve hook
# sh = two small marks
# th = two small hook marks
# Vowels are shown only as a dot at one of several heights beside the consonant (not clearly visible as distinct dots in these four strips).
# Confidence: LOW. The printed alphabet gives many consonants very similar small hook/curl/loop shapes that are not
# reliably distinguishable from each other at this image resolution and in an unfamiliar shorthand hand, and the
# printed instructions state consonants run together in one continuous stroke per word without lifting the pen,
# so individual letters within a joined mark could not be confidently separated in most words. Only the few strokes
# that are simple, distinct straight lines or open curves (a vertical bar for t, a forward slash for r, an open
# parenthesis for d, a backslash for f/v) were matched with any confidence; all other signs are recorded as "?".
